gold.taskTitle: Research Carpentry Apprenticeship Programs Near You
gold.taskDescription: Research available apprenticeship programs in carpentry to find suitable opportunities for training and entry into the trade.

questions.title: What country and region are you located in?
questions.description: Location determines which programs, unions, and governing bodies are relevant to the search.

questions.title: Are you a complete beginner or do you have some carpentry experience?
questions.description: Current skill level affects which tier or type of apprenticeship is appropriate.

questions.title: What specific type of carpentry interests you most?
questions.description: Carpentry has specializations such as rough framing, finish carpentry, cabinetmaking, and formwork, each with different program pathways.

questions.title: Are you open to union-sponsored programs like the UBC?
questions.description: Union versus non-union apprenticeships differ in structure, pay scale, and job placement opportunities.

questions.title: Do you need the program to offer paid work while you train?
questions.description: Some apprenticeships are earn-while-you-learn, while others require unpaid or part-time classroom study periods.

questions.title: What is your target start date for the apprenticeship?
questions.description: Timeline affects which programs have open enrollment and how urgently applications need to be submitted.

questions.title: What will you do with this research when it is complete?
questions.description: Knowing the end goal, such as applying immediately, comparing options, or presenting to someone else, shapes how the research should be organized and how deep it needs to go.
